title: Polynomial Space Constructibility
statement: For every natural number $c$ with $1\leq c$, the function $n\mapsto n^c+1$ is space constructible: for every $n$, its logarithmic space bound is at most $n^c+1$, and there exist a positive natural number $d$ and a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet that, on every Boolean input $x$, outputs the binary representation of $|x|^c+1$ using at most $d(|x|^c+1)$ work-tape cells.
replaced:

constructible: for every $n$, its logarithmic space bound is at most $n^c+1$, and there
are a positive natural number $d$ and a finite Turing machine that, on every Boolean
input $x$, outputs the binary representation of $|x|^c+1$ while using at most
$d(|x|^c+1)$ work-tape cells.
